title: Pre-Analysis (Closed) — Windshield Drained Bracket, Side Window Extension Question
abstract: Closed pre-analysis triggered by side window removals that did not fall after the windshield work, establishing that the same pocket geometry existed at the side window and handing the change to the design office.

sections.objective: Establish why side window removal rates had not fallen after the windshield drained bracket entered service, and whether the same standard could be extended to the side window interface.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed. Nine returned side window assemblies showed the same moisture pattern at the aft lower corner, and the web there carries a comparable pocket that the windshield work never covered — that finding is what made the extension a design task rather than an investigation. The corrosion inspection bulletin covers the windshield frame land only, so aircraft with side window corrosion have no equivalent record. The delamination repair scheme for the web exists but is temporary and limited by flight hours, which means the population is being carried on a repair rather than fixed. The crew limitation entry treats windshields and side windows together, so any extension changes one entry rather than two. The work was handed to the design office and became the second issue launched in late 2025.
sections.next_steps: Delegated to the design office. The resulting change was launched as a second issue extending the bracket and sealing standard to the side window interface.

expected_findings.rationale: The corrosion inspection bulletin covers the windshield frame land only. Aircraft with the same condition at the side window corner have no inspection record and no acceptance limits.
expected_findings.resolution: Extend the inspection bulletin to the side window corner when the design change is released.

expected_findings.rationale: The frame land blend scheme may be applied once per corner. Aircraft that have already used it at the windshield corner cannot use it again if the side window work disturbs the same region.
expected_findings.resolution: State the once-per-corner limit explicitly in the design change accomplishment.

expected_findings.rationale: The windshield bulletin is embodied at a windshield change, and the side window work would be embodied at a side window change; on most aircraft those are different visits, which doubles the sealing work and the cure time.
expected_findings.resolution: Offer a combined accomplishment for operators willing to do both glazing positions at once.

evidence.similarity_note: The crew limitation covers windshields and side windows in one entry, in crew vocabulary, with no reference to brackets, sealant or drainage.

expected_findings.rationale: Because the entry treats both glazing positions together, a change at either position touches the same crew text, which simplifies the documentation impact but means flight operations must be consulted once for both.
expected_findings.resolution: Consult flight operations once, covering both positions, when the design change is launched.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned because it is a window frame repair with similar limits language, but it covers the cabin window intercostal, a different structure with a different load path and no shared identifier with the flight compartment glazing.

type_data.conclusion: Closed and delegated to the design office; the extension was launched as a second issue.
